evidence.source: Adam Khoo — US Stocks Crash? Midterm Election Rally Dead? (Nov 2)
evidence.claim: Post-midterm history: avg +8.1% over next 3 months, 95% positive (19 midterms, only 2018 negative); pre-election dips bottom Oct/early Nov seasonally
evidence.relation: election uncertainty resolves -> risk-on flows; seasonal pattern

evidence.claim: Hedge funds de-grossed -7.8% last week, biggest in 10 years; 6 prior >5% de-grossings all coincided with S&P lows and all were up 1/3/6 months later
evidence.relation: forced deleveraging exhausts sellers -> sell pressure dries up near bottom

evidence.claim: Q3 earnings +30.2% aggregate vs +29% expected; breadth broadening (non-Mag7 earnings growth 32% vs Mag7 22%); S&P net margin 17% (AI cost savings real)
evidence.relation: earnings breadth + margin expansion -> index-level earnings-driven returns

evidence.claim: S&P forward PE 18.7 vs 5yr avg 19.8 and 10yr avg 19.1; cheaper than Jan's 22x (earnings grew faster than price)
evidence.relation: below-average multiple -> less downside risk, earnings-driven upside

evidence.claim: His floor call: at worst a break to 716 (-8% from highs, below a correction), then rally to year-end and next year

evidence.source: Adam Khoo — Will Rising Long Term Rates Crash Stocks? (Sep 14)
evidence.claim: 10-year yield ~4.9% is at/below the 76-year mean 5.52% (median 4.72%); the 1980s decade averaged a 10.6% yield while the S&P compounded +17%/yr — high long rates have historically coexisted with strong bull markets; what matters is the speed of the rise and whether earnings grow alongside
evidence.relation: yield at historical norm + rising earnings → no structural multiple crash

resolution: Yesterday's bearish-leaning resolution was anchored by the ceasefire-break leg (raw up-prob 38.3) that rolled off today's basket with the Nov market, so SPY's prior is now the neutral 50% and the view is evidence-only. Khoo's earnings-breadth/margin fact (lr 1.34, applied) and the Sep-14 rate-normalcy analogue meet no opposing market leg now — prior 50 → posterior 60.7, bullish (low confidence). This is a mechanical revert, not new information: the policy/geopolitical regime is simply unmeasured for SPY today, so the bear risk is absent from the model rather than resolved — if the ceasefire market returns with break odds over 55% or a CPI/hike leg maps onto SPY at hawkish odds, the 2018 analogue (seasonality loses to policy shocks) argues the flip back. Confidence stays low precisely because no market leg corroborates the evidence side.
